doc.title: Peter Ecklund interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: His Arbors album and writing original music
summary: He plans another Arbors Jazz album of mostly original instrumentals, credits Mat Domber, and notes traditional jazz players rarely write new tunes.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Any plans for recording coming up soon? You mentioned your own project.

Yeah. Well I’m doing another album for Arbors Jazz, which is kind of a mixture of, it’s mostly original music actually, and it’s music inspired by situations I’ve been in and it’s all instrumental of course, but it’s music that seems to be pretty conservative to me but it’s not exactly old jazz, it’s not exactly anything, it’s kind of mixture of things. I did an album like that for Arbors, which I really respect Mat Domber for encouraging me to do that, because it’s not exactly the kind of music he has, although it’s really pretty conservative. And I don’t know that it sold a lot but it got some nice reviews so I’ll continue in that direction. I try to perform that music as much as I can, of course I can’t do it here, or I might try one piece in my own set which is coming up later.
Well it’s nice to be able to write your own stuff and have an outlet for it too, because someone should be writing tunes for the future.

Well that’s one odd thing about traditional jazz is that no one does it. I mean every other kind of music I played, everyone did that as a matter of course, and no one thought very much of it either but for some reason it’s like you only play the great songs of the ‘20s, ‘30s, and ‘40s.
Yeah. I suppose they’re looking out there at the audience.
